title: The Castaways of the Mysterious Island
text:
In Jules Verne's novel, five prisoners of war escaped from besieged Richmond in 1865 during the American Civil War by stealing a balloon. A storm carried them far over the Pacific, and the balloon came down on an unknown island. They had almost nothing: the clothes they wore, a notebook, a watch, and a dog named Top.

They were the engineer Cyrus Smith, a man of great scientific knowledge; the journalist Gideon Spilett; the sailor Pencroft, practical and full of energy; Herbert, a teenage boy who knew natural history; and Neb, Smith's devoted companion. They decided to work as one.

When they had no matches, Smith made a lens from the glasses of two watches and lit a fire from the sun. Herbert identified plants and animals for food. Pencroft built boats. Together they made bricks and pottery, smelted iron, produced chemicals and explosives, and even built a telegraph line. Over the years they turned the island into a small, organized colony, helped from time to time by a mysterious protector who turned out to be Captain Nemo.

At last the island's volcano erupted and destroyed almost everything they had built. The colonists, clinging to the last rock above the sea, were rescued by a passing ship.
lesson: A group that pools its knowledge can build a great deal from almost nothing. Each person's skill becomes far more valuable when it is combined with the others'.
people: Cyrus Smith, Gideon Spilett, Pencroft, Herbert, Neb, Captain Nemo
location: France (novel set on a fictional Pacific island)
source: Jules Verne, The Mysterious Island (L'Ile mysterieuse), 1874 to 1875
